official.deadline_note: No central deadline. Nuffic's page directs applicants to the website of the institution they want to apply to for the specific deadline(s); each participating institution sets its own closing date, eligible fields of study and application route (Utrecht University states 1 February 23:59 CET for its round; Radboud University states 31 January 2027 for the 2027-2028 round).
official.application_cycle: Annual cycle run per institution. Nuffic's page currently publishes the participating institutions for the 2026-2027 academic year and states the 2026-2027 application opened on 1 November 2025, while some institutions already run the 2027-2028 round with their own dates.
official.status_note: Nuffic states 'The application for the academic year 2026-2027 opened on 1 November 2025' and 'The list of participating universities changes every year'; participating institutions and their deadlines are published on the institutions' own websites, and several have already opened the next intake round.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The scholarship amounts to EUR 5,000. You will receive this in the first year of your studies. Please note that this is not a full-tuition scholarship.
official.funding_period: one-off, received in the first year of study
benefits: The scholarship amounts to EUR 5,000, received in the first year of your studies
Financed by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science as well as several Dutch research universities and universities of applied sciences
eligibility: You are applying for a full-time bachelor's or master's programme at one of the participating Dutch higher education institutions
You meet the specific requirements of the institution of your choice (set out on the institution's website)
You do not have a degree from an education institution in the Netherlands
requirements: Apply through the participating institution of your choice and meet that institution's specific requirements
Comply with Nuffic's Code of Conduct for Integrity and the situations it defines as unacceptable behaviour
coverage: One-off award of EUR 5,000 received in the first year of studies
application_method: Pick a participating Dutch higher education institution from the annual list Nuffic publishes (the list changes every year)
Check the institution's website for the specific deadline(s) and the fields of study it offers the scholarship for
Apply through that institution's own application process
official.application_route: Apply directly to a participating Dutch institution; Nuffic publishes the annual participant list, but each institution runs its own application, deadline and eligible fields of study.
official.study_mode: full-time (published criterion: a full-time bachelor's or master's programme)
official.citizenship_residency: Non-EEA nationality required; you must not have a degree from an education institution in the Netherlands
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scholarship is meant for international students from outside the European Economic Area (EEA)
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Full-time bachelor's or master's programme at a participating Dutch research university or university of applied sciences; the eligible fields of study are set by each institution
official.description: The NL Scholarship (formerly known as Holland Scholarship) is meant for international students from outside the European Economic Area (EEA) who want to do their bachelor's or master's in the Netherlands. It is financed by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science as well as several Dutch research universities and universities of applied sciences, and amounts to EUR 5,000 received in the first year of studies - explicitly not a full-tuition scholarship.
official.program_type: Government-funded partial scholarship (Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science with participating Dutch research universities and universities of applied sciences)

verification.notes: EUR 5,000 amount, first-year payment and the 'not a full-tuition scholarship' wording confirmed on Nuffic's Study in NL page; per-institution deadlines and the current cycle mix (2026-2027 national list vs 2027-2028 rounds at some institutions) confirmed on Utrecht and Radboud university pages.

applicant_utility.summary: The NL Scholarship pays non-EEA students a one-off EUR 5,000 in their first year at a participating Dutch institution, and Nuffic states plainly that it is not a full-tuition scholarship. There is no central application: you apply through the institution you pick, which sets its own deadline, eligible programmes and sometimes its own award amount (Utrecht, for instance, advertises EUR 5,000-15,000). Treat it as a helpful first-year contribution, not a funding plan, and budget the remaining tuition and living costs yourself.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EEA students already targeting a full-time bachelor's or master's at one of the institutions on Nuffic's current participating list who want a modest first-year contribution rather than full funding.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your target institution appears on the participating list Nuffic publishes for the current academic year - the list changes every year
Open that institution's own NL Scholarship page and note its deadline, eligible programmes and its award amount, which can exceed the EUR 5,000 national minimum
Verify you hold no degree from a Dutch institution (an exchange period alone does not disqualify you, per Utrecht's published wording)
Prepare whatever the institution's own scholarship application asks for - forms, motivation and financial-plan evidence differ per institution
common_rejection_risks: Choosing a programme the institution has excluded from the NL Scholarship, since not all programmes participate
Missing the institution's own deadline, because there is no central deadline to fall back on
Assuming the award covers tuition or living costs when the awarding body states it is not a full-tuition scholarship
Holding an EU/EEA passport or a prior Dutch degree, both of which disqualify you outright
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Everything beyond EUR 5,000: the remainder of tuition and all living costs - Radboud University states that the costs of living and studying in the Netherlands are not covered by the scholarship.
document_audit: Nuffic publishes no central document list; required documents are whatever your chosen institution specifies
Utrecht's process runs inside the applicant's own OSIRIS application account with a separate NL Scholarship step - do not expect a national application form
Where a financial plan is required (Utrecht's Statement of Financial Resources), it must realistically cover the full nominal duration of the programme
alerts: The participating-institution list is refreshed annually, so last year's participant may not award it this year
Deadlines cluster around late January to early February but differ per institution and per intake year, and institutions switch cycles at different times - always check the current round
A few institutions set amounts above EUR 5,000, so the same scholarship can be worth more at one institution than another
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit your degree application to the institution and complete its NL Scholarship step in the institution's own portal before that institution's deadline; Nuffic runs no separate application.

official.deadline_note: TU Delft advises applying before whichever comes first, the MSc programme application deadline or the scholarship deadline; all required documents, including GRE and English test results, must be uploaded before the deadline. Missing the scholarship deadline means the scholarship application will not be reviewed.
official.application_cycle: 2027-2029 round (Scholarship Application Form 2027-2029 for a two-year MSc starting September 2027)
official.status_note: TU Delft is running the current round with the Scholarship Application Form 2027-2029 and a scholarship deadline of 1 December 2026 (23:59 CET); students who have been granted a scholarship are informed by TU Delft via email by the end of March 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Awarded students will receive full tuition fees per year for a TU Delft MSc programme based on the Statutory or Institutional rate, according to the registered nationality.
official.funding_period: per academic year (2 yrs); living allowance monthly x24
benefits: Full tuition fees for the first year for a TU Delft MSc programme (statutory fee or institutional rate, according to the registered nationality)
A contribution for the living expenses - a fixed monthly living allowance stated in the scholarship contract
Second-year tuition and living allowances, conditional on completing at least 48 ECTS out of 60 by the end of the first academic year
eligibility: Excellent international applicant (conditionally) admitted to one of the 2-year regular TU Delft MSc programmes (not an International Joint Education Programme)
Excellent academic results in previous study programme(s) relevant to the master's applied for; as an indication, amongst the top 10% of graduates - proof of ranking is not required
Complete MSc application submitted before the scholarship deadline
Not a TU Delft BSc student (including international students), bachelor's degree not obtained at a Dutch university, and not already started MSc studies at TU Delft
Not older than 35 years at the start of the first academic year at TU Delft (1 September)
requirements: Complete MSc application submitted before the scholarship deadline (diploma, transcript, English language certificate, motivation letter, CV, proof of identity)
Scholarship Application Form (SAF) 2027-2029 submitted at the same time as the MSc application
One reference letter (if you have two references, uploaded as one PDF)
English language certificate included with the MSc application before the scholarship deadline, unless exempt
documents: Complete TU Delft MSc application (diploma, transcript, English language certificate, motivation letter, CV, proof of identity)
One reference letter (two references merged into a single PDF)
Dutch bank account details after enrolment, needed for the first scholarship payment
selection_criteria: Scholarship selection takes place only after the admission office has given a positive assessment; TU Delft faculty selection committees make the final selection
Scholarships are extremely limited and highly competitive, with only the strongest candidates selected
Academic excellence in the previous programme(s), relevant to the master's applied for (top 10% indicated; proof of ranking not required)
coverage: Full tuition fees for the first year, based on the statutory fee or institutional rate according to the registered nationality
Contribution for the living expenses (a monthly contribution for 24 months, per the FAQ)
Second-year tuition and living allowances if at least 48 of 60 ECTS are completed in the first academic year
Flight tickets, accommodation and extra allowances are not covered; these must be arranged and paid by the student
application_method: Complete the MSc application and check the admission requirements
Upload the Scholarship Application Form 2027-2029 together with the application
Upload one reference letter (two references as one PDF) and the English language certificate before the scholarship deadline
official.application_route: Apply through the TU Delft international MSc application, uploading the Scholarship Application Form 2027-2029, one reference letter and the English language certificate before 1 December 2026 (23:59 CET)
official.study_mode: Full-time, 2-year regular TU Delft MSc programme
official.citizenship_residency: For excellent international applicants; it is not possible to apply as an EU citizen and be considered for a scholarship available to non-EU citizens, including with dual EU/non-EU nationality
official.international_eligibility: Yes - for excellent international students (conditionally) admitted to a regular 2-year TU Delft MSc programme
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All regular 2-year TU Delft MSc programmes except Metropolitan Analysis, Design and Engineering; Applied Geophysics; The Berlage Post-master; Industrial Ecology; and Geographical Information Management and Applications; International Joint Education Programmes are excluded
official.duration: Two years (24 months); extensions beyond the 2-year period are not supported by the scholarship
official.description: The Justus & Louise van Effen Excellence Scholarships are financed by the legacy of Justus and Louise van Effen and awarded by TU Delft - 16 full scholarships for the regular MSc programmes, two per faculty. Awarded students receive full tuition fees per year for a TU Delft MSc programme, based on the statutory or institutional rate according to their registered nationality, plus a contribution towards living expenses.
official.program_type: University excellence scholarship financed by the legacy of Justus and Louise van Effen
official.english_requirement: All applicants who wish to be considered for a scholarship are required to include their English test with their MSc application before the scholarship deadline; exempt applicants do not need it. The required level follows the chosen MSc programme - no single score is published on the scholarship page.

not_confirmed: specific English test scores (set per MSc programme)
verification.notes: Coverage wording, 1 December 2026 (23:59 CET) deadline, eligibility rules, programme exclusions and terms confirmed on TU Delft's scholarships and FAQ pages. TU Delft publishes no euro figure for this award ('the value of different scholarships may vary'), so funding_amount is null; the URL given in the brief returns 404 and the live official page is the scholarships page cited above.

applicant_utility.summary: TU Delft awards two Justus & Louise van Effen Excellence Scholarships per faculty - full tuition for both years of a regular MSc plus a monthly living contribution - but only to applicants whose complete MSc application is uploaded by 1 December 2026. The euro value is deliberately not published; what TU Delft does publish is the structure: tuition at your nationality's statutory or institutional rate, a fixed monthly living allowance for 24 months, and loss of all second-year support if you complete fewer than 48 of 60 ECTS. Flights, accommodation and insurance remain your own cost.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Top-decile international applicants with a profile strong enough for conditional admission to a regular two-year TU Delft MSc, who can assemble every document in a single December round.
application_readiness_checklist: Book the English test early and upload the result with the MSc application before 1 December - a certificate arriving later cannot be considered
Ask referees early: one reference letter must arrive before the deadline, with two referees merged into a single PDF
Download the Scholarship Application Form 2027-2029 from TU Delft's file list and upload it together with the MSc application
Check your target MSc is a regular 2-year TU Delft programme and not one of the five excluded ones or a joint programme
Plan Dutch bank account details and settle-in funds for September-October, since the first living payment only arrives after enrolment and physical presence in the Netherlands
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 1 December scholarship deadline - TU Delft states the scholarship application then will not be reviewed at all
An incomplete MSc application: diploma, transcript, English certificate, motivation letter, CV or proof of identity missing at the deadline
Holding or expecting any other partial or full scholarship funding, which TU Delft prohibits alongside this award
Being a TU Delft BSc student, holding a Dutch bachelor's degree, or having already started MSc studies at TU Delft
Being older than 35 on 1 September at the start of the first academic year
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Flight tickets, accommodation and insurance are explicitly not covered; expect to self-fund roughly EUR 1,500 of settle-in costs (TU Delft's own approximate figure) and to bridge September-October before the first living payment.
document_audit: The Scholarship Application Form must be uploaded at the same time as the MSc application - a later submission is not reviewed
Two reference letters must be merged into one PDF; separate uploads break the requirement
The English certificate counts only if uploaded before the scholarship deadline, even though the admission decision may still be pending
If awarded, you must submit the confirmation statement before the scholarship can be officially awarded
alerts: Admission and scholarship selection are sequential - you are only considered after a positive admission assessment, yet every document must still be uploaded by 1 December
Only winners are emailed (by end of March); silence means rejection, as TU Delft sends no rejection notice
The scholarship cannot be combined with any other partial or full scholarship funding
Second-year money depends on completing 48 of 60 ECTS - falling behind costs you the entire second-year package
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One combined round: submit the complete MSc application with the SAF 2027-2029, reference letter and English certificate uploaded before 1 December 2026 23:59 CET; TU Delft then assesses admission and scholarship in sequence and emails awardees by end of March 2027.
